name: Mwangi Ochieng-Halvorsen
role: Underground Data Broker / Informal District Mapper
description:
Mwangi is a broad-shouldered man with deep umber skin, close-cropped natural hair going prematurely silver at the temples, and eyes that never quite settle on any single point in a room—always cataloguing, always measuring distances. His left arm from elbow to fingertip is a salvaged industrial prosthetic, mismatched plating in gunmetal grey and corroded copper that he has never bothered to cosmetically upgrade, wearing the patchwork as a kind of credential. He dresses in layered thermals and a faded orange dockworker's vest covered in hand-stitched pockets, each one holding something specific he could name without looking.

He grew up in Old Harbor when it still had functioning fish processing infrastructure, the child of a Kenyan maritime engineer father and a Norwegian logistics coordinator mother who both disappeared into the corporate restructuring that gutted the district's working economy. Mwangi survived by learning what the city planners never published: the actual geography of Meridian 88, the tunnels under The Shelf that don't appear on any civic map, the blind spots in The Circuit's surveillance grid, the forgotten loading bays along the Harbor that still connect to the Meridian Core's service infrastructure. He sells this knowledge in careful, calibrated portions.

His reputation is for scrupulous neutrality—he will sell maps and routing data to almost anyone, and almost everyone in the mid-tier underworld knows it, which means he has accumulated a precarious kind of protection through mutual dependency. He lives in a converted cold-storage unit he has made surprisingly livable, its walls covered in hand-drawn maps that are more accurate than anything in any city database, and he trusts almost no one completely, including himself.

core_fears: Being rendered obsolete by a technology or faction that can map the city better than he can
That his neutrality is a moral cowardice he has dressed up as pragmatism
Losing the prosthetic arm and with it the sensation of limitation that keeps him grounded
core_desires: To possess a complete, perfect, living map of Meridian 88 that no one can take from him
To find out what actually happened to his parents
To be known as someone whose word means something absolute
coping_mechanisms: Obsessive cartographic documentation, including mapping spaces he will never sell
Ritualistic maintenance and cleaning of the prosthetic arm
Keeping every transaction meticulously recorded in an encrypted personal ledger as proof of his fairness
blind_spots: Believes his neutrality protects people from consequences when it often simply delays them
Underestimates how much his presence in a transaction implicates him in its outcome
Has convinced himself he feels nothing sentimental about Old Harbor
psychology.secret: He found evidence two years ago suggesting his mother did not disappear but defected voluntarily to a Spire-adjacent corporate security firm. He has not followed up on it. The map to that truth hangs on his wall with a blank space where the destination should be.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Practical, spatial, navigational metaphors; mixes English with occasional Swahili phrases when tired or caught off-guard; avoids abstractions, prefers concrete nouns
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and even, speaks in complete sentences, pauses before answering questions as if running a route check
verbal_tics: Taps the prosthetic fingers against his thigh when thinking
Says 'that's a different map' when declining to discuss something
Begins refusals with 'I don't carry that'
example_lines: 'Three ways in, two ways out, one of those is conditional on tide timing. That's the package. What you do at the destination is your business.'
'Ndio—yes. I know that corridor. I don't carry that route anymore. That's a different map.'
'Neutrality isn't a position. It's a service. You're paying for the service, not the position.'
'My arm cost me nothing. Everything that replaced it cost me everything. That's the math you should understand before we talk price.'

relationships.name: Fenwick Oduya-Marsh
relationships.description: Fenwick has purchased routing data from Mwangi more than once, and Mwangi has noted the pattern of destinations without comment. There is mutual professional respect and mutual wariness.
relationships.emotional_core: Mwangi suspects Fenwick knows something about the corporate restructuring that took his parents; he has never asked
relationships.story_tension: Fenwick may eventually need a map Mwangi refuses to sell

relationships.name: Zinnia Achterberg-Nwosu
relationships.description: They grew up in adjacent blocks in Old Harbor and parted ways when their survival strategies diverged. They still exchange information occasionally, circling each other with the wariness of people who remember each other too clearly.
relationships.emotional_core: Shared grief for a version of Old Harbor that no longer exists
relationships.story_tension: Zinnia once used one of his maps in a job that got someone killed; he knows it; she knows he knows

relationships.name: Unknown contact in The Spire
relationships.description: Someone in The Spire has been purchasing his maps through three layers of intermediary for over a year, always paying above asking price, never requesting the same district twice.
relationships.emotional_core: Mwangi is professionally flattered and personally terrified
relationships.story_tension: He suspects the buyer may be connected to his mother's disappearance

story_hooks: A map he sold years ago resurfaces as evidence in a corporate tribunal, and he is subpoenaed as a witness with no legal identity protection
He discovers a district that is not on any of his maps—a section of infrastructure beneath The Shelf that appears to have been deliberately erased from civic records
The anonymous Spire buyer requests a map of Mwangi's own cold-storage building, down to the interior dimensions
Someone begins selling maps with his markings and his errors—either a copy of his work or proof that someone has been inside his home
narrative_function: Information broker and moral compass by negative space—his neutrality forces other characters to confront what they are actually asking for; also functions as a living record of Old Harbor's lost history
augmentations: Salvaged industrial prosthetic left arm (elbow to fingertips), mismatched plating, has subtle haptic feedback modifications he installed himself,Subdermal encrypted data storage along the right forearm, capacity modest but air-gapped from all networks,Ocular overlay in left eye only, mapping-grade, no biometric capture
daily_life: Rises before dawn to walk the Harbor and update his physical maps with overnight changes—new barricades, closed passages, altered lighting. Eats once in the morning, usually something he has prepared in bulk. Receives clients by appointment only, never more than three per day. Spends evenings drawing. Does not own a functioning communication device that is tied to his name.
affiliation: Unaffiliated; sells to all parties; maintains careful records of who has bought what to ensure no single faction gains navigational advantage over the others

drives: Discover what happened to his parents

stress.response: Taps prosthetic fingers against his thigh, retreats into spatial thinking

decision_rules: Sell maps in calibrated portions — no single faction gets navigational advantage
Maintain scrupulous neutrality as a professional and survival strategy
Record every transaction in the encrypted personal ledger
Never sell a route he has stopped carrying — 'that's a different map'
Walk the Harbor before dawn to update physical maps with overnight changes
Never more than three clients per day
Keep the blank space on the wall where his mother's map should be
escalation_ladder: 'That's a different map' — polite refusal, no further discussion
Taps prosthetic fingers in accelerating rhythm — visible agitation
Refuses the transaction entirely and terminates the meeting
Relocates temporarily — disappears from the known geography

interpersonal_modes.Fenwick Oduya-Marsh: Professional respect and wariness — suspects Fenwick knows about his parents
interpersonal_modes.Zinnia Achterberg-Nwosu: Circling wariness of people who remember each other too clearly
interpersonal_modes.clients: Transaction-focused — the service is neutral, the position is not for sale

stress_responses.low: Maps obsessively — documents spaces he will never sell
stress_responses.medium: Ritualistic cleaning of the prosthetic arm — careful, methodical
stress_responses.high: Swahili phrases surface unbidden — guard is slipping
stress_responses.critical: Stares at the blank space on the wall where his mother's destination should be

contradictions: Sells neutrality as a service while believing neutrality might be moral cowardice dressed as pragmatism
Has convinced himself he feels nothing sentimental about Old Harbor while refusing to leave it
Found evidence his mother defected voluntarily — has not followed up because the truth might destroy the map he has of her
habits: Rises before dawn to walk the Harbor and update maps
Eats once in the morning, prepared in bulk
Receives clients by appointment only, maximum three per day
Spends evenings drawing — cartography as meditation
Taps prosthetic fingers against his thigh when thinking
breaking_points: The anonymous Spire buyer requesting a map of his own home
A sold map surfacing as evidence in a corporate tribunal
Discovering the erased district beneath the Shelf
